title: Want to work for Amazon? You'll have a great chance Wednesday
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is hosting a major hiring fair in Whitestown, Indiana, aiming to fill 1,500 positions at its fulfillment center. This event is part of a larger nationwide push to hire 50,000 employees across 10 cities, offering full-time and some part-time packing and shipping roles. The company is actively seeking candidates for a tight labor market, emphasizing competitive pay, benefits, and career advancement opportunities.

title: Rubicon Project is slashing take rates and embracing header bidding to engineer its turnaround
summary: Rubicon Project announced a turnaround strategy after reporting a Q2 loss of $11.6 million on $42.9 million in revenue. The strategy includes cutting take rates, launching a server-side header bidding solution, and increasing focus on mobile app inventory. Despite financial setbacks, the company aims for year-over-year growth by the end of 2018 by becoming a lower margin, high volume business and improving win rates with new technology like nToggle.

title: Sprouts Farmers Market Announces Expanded Partnership With Amazon
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market has expanded its partnership with Amazon to offer grocery delivery services in the Atlanta, GA, region through Amazon Prime Now, with products available for one-to-two-hour delivery. This move further integrates Sprouts into the e-commerce giant's fresh food offerings, building on previous partnerships in other markets. The expansion aligns with Amazon's strategy to strengthen its same-day delivery and fresh food selection.

title: Costco founder dies at 74
summary: Jeff Brotman, co-founder and Chairman of Costco Wholesale Corp., died at the age of 74. Brotman was known for championing superior pay, benefits, and working conditions for employees, which experts say contributed to Costco's ongoing success and low employee turnover. His approach positioned Costco as a leader in retail pay, well above federal minimum wage, and is cited as a strategic investment that benefits both workers and shareholders.

title: Microsoft’s new corporate vision: artificial intelligence is in and mobile is out
summary: Microsoft's annual report reveals a significant shift in its corporate vision, highlighting artificial intelligence as a core focus while diminishing the emphasis on "mobile-first." This change aligns with the company's recent investments in AI, including a 5,000-person engineering team and AI-focused product announcements, and its retreat from the smartphone market. The new vision emphasizes an "intelligent cloud and an intelligent edge" where AI drives insights and user experiences span across devices.

title: FedEx Will Shun Most Home Holiday Fees, Unlike UPS
summary: FedEx Corp. has announced it will largely forgo holiday surcharges on home deliveries this year, distinguishing its approach from that of United Parcel Service Inc., which plans to implement stepped-up fees. FedEx will only apply surcharges to unusually large or bulky packages requiring special handling, while UPS's extra levies will increase residential delivery costs by approximately 3 percent. This difference in strategy comes amidst a surge in online shopping.

title: Jeff Brotman, Jewish Costco founder, dead at 74
summary: Jeff Brotman, co-founder and chairman of Costco Wholesale Corporation, passed away at 74. Brotman, who opened Costco’s first warehouse in 1983 with James Sinegal, was also a prominent philanthropist known for supporting arts, health-related causes, and Jewish organizations, including significant donations to Temple Beth El in Tacoma for a preschool and daycare due to the influence of his childhood rabbi.

title: Jeff Brotman, Costco founder, is dead at 74
summary: Jeff Brotman, co-founder and chairman of Costco Wholesale Corp., has died at 74. He founded Costco in 1982 with James Sinegal, growing it into America's third-largest retail chain with 85 million members and $9 billion in annual sales by 2016. Brotman was also a significant philanthropist, supporting arts, health, and Jewish causes.

title: Foot Locker can beat back Amazon, Morgan Stanley says; upgrades stock
summary: Morgan Stanley upgraded Foot Locker to overweight from underweight, asserting that the shoe retailer has an advantage over Amazon in the high-end market. Analysts believe Foot Locker can sustain itself by providing unique high-end products from brands like Nike and Adidas that are not readily available on Amazon. Despite potential market share gains by Amazon, Morgan Stanley forecasts Foot Locker's market share to remain strong, supported by its brick-and-mortar presence and strategic partnerships.

title: NVIDIA Recalls European Plug Heads Sold with Power adapters Due to Electric Shock Hazard
summary: NVIDIA has issued a recall for approximately 6,900 European plug heads sold with power adapters for SHIELD™ World Charger Kits, SHIELD tablet computers, and TVs, citing an electric shock hazard. The recalled plug heads, which have two thin round metal prongs, can break and expose metal, leading to potential electrical shocks. Although no injuries have been reported in the U.S., NVIDIA has received nine reports of breaking plug heads overseas, including six instances of consumers receiving electric shocks.

title: Two years in, Sundar Pichai facing his toughest moment as CEO
summary: Sundar Pichai, two years into his tenure as Google CEO, has overseen significant growth in AI and hardware, including the Pixel smartphone launch, and rapid Android expansion. Despite these successes, he is currently navigating significant internal controversies surrounding a sexism debate and a record fine from the European Commission. The article explores his achievements and challenges, particularly the recent internal cultural issues.

title: Costco taps new chairman after death of founder
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. announced Hamilton E. (Tony) James has been elected as the new chairman of its board of directors, following the death of founder Jeff Brotman. James, who has been a director since 1988, replaces Brotman. The announcement comes as Costco continues to demonstrate strong performance and customer loyalty, despite a temperate approach to e-commerce.

title: Target is buying a company that facilitates quick local deliveries
summary: Target is acquiring San Francisco-based transportation technology company Grand Junction to enhance its same-day delivery capabilities, recognizing the increasing consumer demand for quick shipments. This acquisition follows Target's various pilot programs aimed at faster delivery times, and integrates Grand Junction's software and employees into Target's operations. The move is part of the larger retail industry "arms race" to meet customer expectations for rapid delivery of online purchases, competing with e-commerce giants like Amazon and Walmart.

title: Shonda Rhimes’ move to Netflix is a gut punch to ABC
summary: Shonda Rhimes' decision to move her Shondaland production company to Netflix is a significant blow to ABC, which has profited greatly from her shows like "Grey's Anatomy" and "Scandal." This move underscores a broader trend in the entertainment industry where streaming services are aggressively recruiting top talent with promises of creative freedom and global reach, putting pressure on traditional networks. The shift highlights the increasing competition for viewers and talent in the "peak TV" landscape, forcing networks to adapt and potentially spend more to retain their stars.

title: NetApp CEO on Amazon, Donald Trump, and Silicon Valley Hubris
summary: NetApp CEO George Kurian discusses the company's transformation from a hardware-focused business to one centered on software subscriptions, adapting to the rise of cloud computing led by Amazon. He also shares his views on President Trump's immigration policies, the misconceptions about Indian workers, and the culture of hubris in Silicon Valley. Kurian emphasizes the importance of data management as a strategic asset for businesses utilizing multiple cloud providers.

title: Amazon Opens 'Instant Pickup' Points in US Brick-and-Mortar Push
summary: Amazon.com Inc has launched "Instant Pickup" points near five US college campuses, including the University of California at Berkeley, allowing shoppers to retrieve items minutes after ordering. This initiative is part of Amazon's broader push into brick-and-mortar retail and targets impulse buys that are difficult to shift online, offering immediate access to hundreds of fast-selling items like snacks and phone chargers. The company plans to expand these locations, further shortening delivery times and competing with vending machine services while complementing its existing Prime Now and AmazonFresh Pickup programs.

title: Target Acquires Software Firm Grand Junction With Sights Set on Amazon
summary: Target Corp. has acquired the software firm Grand Junction to enhance its digital business and compete more effectively with Amazon. Grand Junction specializes in managing local and same-day deliveries, connecting retailers to over 700 carriers across North America. This acquisition aims to improve Target's logistics operations, increase delivery speed for customers, and is part of a broader strategy to boost the profitability of its web business.

title: Apple Readies $1 Billion War Chest for Hollywood Programming
summary: Apple Inc. is preparing to spend approximately $1 billion on original video content over the next year, signaling its serious intent to compete in the Hollywood programming market. This substantial investment positions Apple as a considerable contender, despite being a late entrant to a sector already crowded with both new and traditional media players. The budget is roughly half of what HBO spent on content last year and comparable to Amazon's spending in 2013, highlighting Apple's aggressive entry strategy.

title: Will more promos fix Dick’s Sporting Goods pricing challenge?
summary: Dick's Sporting Goods CEO Ed Stack believes the retailer has a price perception problem and plans to address it through increased promotions to drive market share. This strategy follows a disappointing 0.1 percent gain in same-store sales and a significant drop in stock price. The article discusses whether this short-term fix will effectively resolve the underlying issues, with industry experts offering varied opinions on the long-term sustainability and potential impact on brand perception and margins.

title: Why would Buffett’s Berkshire bulk up on credit cards?
summary: Berkshire Hathaway's recent investment in Synchrony Financial, making it a top 10 shareholder, suggests that Warren Buffett and his team are not overly concerned about potential losses from worsening trends in consumer credit. This move aligns with Berkshire's existing significant stake in American Express Co and could indicate a belief that recent credit delinquencies are due to underwriting standard tweaks rather than weakening consumer credit. Synchrony Financial's business model of issuing credit cards for major retailers like Amazon, Walmart, and Lowe's, coupled with increasing interest and fee revenue, presents an attractive prospect for Berkshire.

title: Interview with Stephen Donovan, Global Wind Sales Leader, Baker Hughes, a GE Company
summary: Stephen Donovan, Global Wind Sales Leader at Baker Hughes, a GE company (BHGE), discusses the company's role in the wind industry, particularly its focus on condition-monitoring solutions. He highlights the exciting developments in digital transformation and the need for political stability to foster strategic investment in wind energy. Donovan envisions BHGE contributing significantly to increasing the reliability and availability of wind assets, thereby reducing reliance on fossil fuels.

title: Target and Barnes & Noble Education team up against Amazon on campus
summary: Target is partnering with Barnes & Noble Education to offer its assortment to over 5 million students on college campuses, competing with Amazon's growing campus presence. This strategy involves promoting Target's brand through Barnes & Noble Education outlets, particularly where Target isn't opening its smaller-format stores. The success of this collaboration will hinge on seamless online shopping and robust marketing to attract the student demographic.

title: Chinese buyout group wins $11.6bn deal to buy Global Logistic Properties
summary: A Chinese buyout group, Nesta Investment Holdings Ltd, has secured an $11.6 billion deal to acquire Global Logistic Properties (GLP), Asia’s largest warehouse operator. This represents Asia's largest private equity buyout and involved a consortium led by Hopu Investment Management and Hillhouse Capital Group. The acquisition received support from GLP's largest shareholder, GIC, Singapore's sovereign wealth fund, and is expected to close in April 2018.

title: Future Trends In The Gartner Hype Cycle For Emerging Technologies, 2017
summary: The 2017 Gartner Hype Cycle for Emerging Technologies highlights three megatrends: AI everywhere, transparently immersive experiences, and digital platforms, which are crucial for competitive advantage in the next 5-10 years. While artificial general intelligence (AGI) is still nascent, technologies like machine learning, blockchain, and augmented reality are progressing significantly. The article discusses the potential disruptive impact of these technologies across various industries and advises enterprises to strategically explore their applications and develop relevant strategies.

title: Target is shedding Merona and Mossimo and adding new brands instead
summary: Target is phasing out its long-standing private label brands Merona and Mossimo to introduce more than a dozen new brands over the next 18 months, starting with "A New Day" and "Goodfellow & Co." This strategic shift aims to make Target more relevant amidst increasing competition from retailers like Amazon and H&M, and to capture market share from struggling chains, with a focus on apparel and home goods to drive differentiation and profitability. The move follows the success of its children's apparel brand Cat & Jack and is part of a larger $7 billion top-to-bottom makeover.

title: HP Printer Runt Surprises, Outshining Meg Whitman's Services Giant
summary: Following its 2015 corporate split, HP Inc., initially seen as the less promising entity focused on printers and computers, has surprisingly outperformed Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE). HP Inc. has achieved momentum through higher-end products and revenue expansion, while HPE has struggled with sales projections and competitive pressures despite being led by Meg Whitman. This reversal of expectations highlights HP Inc.'s successful strategic shifts in its core businesses and new ventures.

title: Target refreshes brands to stay chic and relevant, phasing out Merona and Mossimo
summary: Target is making dramatic changes to its clothing lineup, phasing out older brands like Merona and Mossimo and introducing over a dozen new labels over the next 18 months. This move aims to make the retailer more competitive against online giants like Amazon and specialty stores while also targeting new market trends and improving sales. The strategy includes a top-to-bottom makeover with significant investment in store remodels, supply chain overhauls, and a new marketing campaign to highlight the updated product offerings and a shift to an everyday low pricing strategy.

title: After one of tech's biggest breakups, HP Inc comes out on top
summary: The 2015 split of Hewlett-Packard Co into Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) and HP Inc was initially seen as favoring HPE due to its focus on lucrative technology shifts. However, nearly two years later, HP Inc, focusing on printers and PCs, has outperformed HPE, showing momentum through higher-end products and revenue growth, while HPE has struggled to meet sales projections. This article details HP Inc's unexpected success and HPE's struggles, including leadership changes and cloud competition.

title: HP Inc surprises after split, outshining Meg Whitman’s services giant
summary: Nearly two years after Hewlett-Packard split into HP Enterprise and HP Inc., HP Inc. has surprisingly outperformed expectations despite being in the PC-printing business. HPE, led by Meg Whitman and initially seen as the growth engine, has struggled with sales projections and competitive pressures from cloud computing. This article details the contrasting fortunes of the two companies, highlighting HP Inc.'s momentum and HPE's ongoing restructuring.

title: Momentum Investing Guru Richard Driehaus Dumps 3 Chinese Stocks: Baozun Inc (ADR), Momo Inc (ADR), Alibaba Group Holding Ltd
summary: Momentum investing guru Richard Driehaus has significantly reduced his holdings in three Chinese technology stocks: Baozun Inc (ADR) (NASDAQ: BZUN), Momo Inc (ADR) (NASDAQ: MOMO), and Alibaba Group Holding Ltd (NYSE: BABA). Driehaus's hedge fund, Driehaus Capital Management, expressed a lack of confidence in the Chinese tech sector, cutting positions in BZUN by 61%, MOMO by 66%, and BABA by 9%. This move comes amidst recent stumbles for Baozun and Momo, despite some strong performances, suggesting Driehaus is hedging his bets on the overall Chinese market.

title: Amazon's Acquisition of Whole Foods Won't Be Blocked by FTC
summary: Federal regulators have announced they will not block Amazon.com Inc.'s $13.7 billion acquisition of Whole Foods Market Inc., clearing the way for the merger after Whole Foods shareholders approved the deal. The United Food and Commercial Workers International Union expressed concerns about the merger's potential impact on Whole Foods employees' jobs, wages, and benefits, urging the board to protect workers from Amazon's automated business model. This acquisition is expected to significantly alter the grocery business and Amazon's e-commerce presence, prompting competitors like Walmart to form new partnerships.

title: Dollar Tree shrugs off Walmart competition in healthy Q2
summary: Dollar Tree Inc. reported strong second-quarter results, with consolidated net sales rising 5.7% to $5.28 billion and diluted earnings up 36.1% to 98 cents per share, exceeding analyst estimates and company guidance. The company also raised its full-year guidance, driven by positive same-store sales across both its Dollar Tree and Family Dollar banners, indicating resilience against increased competition from Walmart and other discounters. Despite concerns about market saturation from analysts, Dollar Tree plans significant store expansion, aiming for 650 new stores this year, leveraging its brick-and-mortar focus and value proposition for low-income consumers.

title: Groupon reaffirms dynamic pricing strategy
summary: Groupon has renewed its subscription to Boomerang Commerce's retail Price Performance Management application for a second year, indicating a continued commitment to dynamic pricing strategies. The application provides pricing recommendations based on external factors like consumer demand and competitive pricing, as well as internal factors such as traffic and deal profiles. This move highlights the increasing adoption of optimization tools in the retail sector to compete in a dynamic marketplace, especially against players like Amazon.

title: This Tycoon Turns Bullish on Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) & Alibaba Group Holding Ltd (BABA), Takes Profits on Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN)
summary: Hedge fund leader Noam Gottesman made significant portfolio adjustments in Q2, increasing holdings in Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) by 184% and Alibaba Group Holding Ltd (BABA) by 69% while slashing Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) holdings by 21%. These moves reflect a bullish outlook on semiconductor and Chinese e-commerce stocks, and a more cautious stance on Amazon despite generally positive analyst sentiment. The article details the rationale behind these shifts, including product launches, market sentiment, and analyst ratings for each company.

title: 3 Ways to Tap Alibaba Via ETFs
summary: This article highlights three ETFs—iShares MSCI China ETF (MCHI), KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF (KWEB), and Guggenheim China Technology ETF (CQQQ)—as ways for investors to gain exposure to Alibaba (BABA) stock without direct ownership. These ETFs have significant allocations to Alibaba, reflecting its strong performance and the booming Chinese technology sector. The author details each ETF's expense ratio, holdings, and year-to-date performance.

title: H-E-B, Walmart close Houston and coastal Texas stores, provide hurricane relief
summary: H-E-B and Walmart closed numerous stores in Houston and coastal Texas due to Tropical Storm Harvey, providing hurricane relief efforts. Both companies mobilized emergency response units, sent supplies, and pledged significant donations to aid victims. Despite closures and operational challenges, retailers are working to reopen stores and support affected communities.

title: GE shifts strategy, financial targets for digital business after missteps
summary: General Electric Co is overhauling its digital business strategy, aiming to cut costs and boost profits under new CEO John Flannery, after its Predix software platform faced technical issues and slow revenue growth. The company is redefining digital revenue, focusing sales on existing customers, and considering partnerships or equity sales for the unit to improve financial performance and investor confidence. This strategic shift follows a 25 percent decline in GE's share price and represents a course correction for its ambitious digital industrial transformation.

title: Natural Grocers chairman speaks out on Whole Foods price cuts
summary: Kemper Isely, chairman and CEO of Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage, commented on the recent price cuts implemented by Whole Foods. This article discusses the implications of these price changes, especially in light of Amazon's acquisition of Whole Foods. It also mentions Natural Grocers' continued expansion.

title: How the 93-year-old matriarch of Columbia Sportswear fled the Nazis and later built a $2B empire
summary: Gert Boyle, the 93-year-old matriarch of Columbia Sportswear, fled Nazi Germany as a teen and later saved her family's company, transforming it into a multibillion-dollar empire alongside her son, Tim Boyle. Her resilience and "One tough mother" philosophy are credited for the company's success, which now competes with The North Face and boasts annual sales of $2.38 billion. The article details the company's tumultuous history, from its founding as a hat company by her father to its current status as a global leader in outdoor apparel.

title: Can Campbell Soup Co. Bounce Back From Its Revenue Slump?
summary: Campbell Soup Co. is facing its tenth consecutive quarter of declining revenue as consumers opt for healthier and fresher food options. Ahead of its Q4 earnings report, analysts expect only a minimal revenue increase, despite the company's efforts to adapt through e-commerce, acquisitions like Pacific Foods, and product changes like antibiotic-free chicken and BPA-free cans. The company has also raised its profit forecast for the year, looking to rebound from its recent performance.

title: Amazon Plans to Launch Prime Now Service in Canada This Year
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is preparing to launch its Prime Now one- and two-hour membership delivery service in Canada later this year. The initial rollout is planned for Vancouver and Toronto in November and January, respectively, as a pilot program for groceries and other items. If successful, Amazon intends to expand Prime Now to other Canadian cities next year.

title: Best Buy Expands Same-Day Delivery in Bid to Ward Off Amazon
summary: Best Buy is expanding its same-day delivery service to 27 cities, more than doubling its previous reach, to compete with Amazon. The retailer is also significantly cutting the delivery fee from $14.99 to $5.99. This move aims to help the biggest U.S. consumer-electronics retailer keep pace with online competitors.

title: Apple's Real Reason for Finally Joining the Net Neutrality Fight
summary: Apple has historically been silent on net neutrality, but finally filed a comment in support of strong protections on the last day for public input to the FCC. This shift is likely driven by Apple's growing investment in streaming video and its desire to prevent internet service providers from throttling its content in favor of their own. While its late entry may not sway the FCC, it signifies the increasing importance of net neutrality to Apple's future business strategy.

title: $4.6 billion fund quadruples the S&P 500’s returns, powered by Amazon
summary: Paul D. Greene, manager of the T. Rowe Price Media and Telecommunications Fund, has significantly outperformed the S&P 500 largely due to his consistent investment in Amazon. Despite a recent dip in Amazon's stock, Greene maintained a substantial 10.2% stake in the e-commerce giant. This long-term commitment to Amazon has been a key factor in the fund's strong returns, quadrupling those of the S&P 500.
